newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk MPs urge police trial for rebel jail deaths.
newsitem.headline: Turk MPs urge police trial for rebel jail deaths.

text.p: Turkey's parliamentary human rights watchdog has called for the trial of almost 70 policemen and soldiers for the beating deaths of 10 Kurdish rebel prisoners in a jail protest this year, commission members said on Wednesday.
"We stressed that these people must be put on trial. They must be put before independent judicial authorities," Demir Berberoglu, the chairman of the human rights commision, told Reuters.

The commission approved proposals by its members for a judicial investigation and said 30 soldiers and 38 policemen should be put on trial for their part in quelling September's disturbance in southeast Turkey's high-security Diyarbakir jail.
Berberoglu said the security forces, armed with shields and batons, used force to break up a protest about food supplies by members of the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
An autopsy released by the commission gave the cause of death of most of the prisoners as "brain damage" but did not explain how the injuries could have occurred.
The bodies had bruising and wounds, the reports said.

Berberoglu, a deputy from the right-wing coalition partner True Path Party (DYP), said the trial should be held outside the emergency rule region in the southeast, where security forces have fought the PKK for the last 12 years.
"This matter is very sensitive and for the trial to be independent and sound it must be held at a place outside the emergency rule region," the MP said.
"There must be an outcome which is satisfying not just for those close to the dead, but for public and international opinion," he said.
Documents on the incident in Diyarbakir prison were sent to Turkey's regional administration board, which must decide whether to pass on the papers for further investigation.
